why: From A to B the whole cross turns 45 degrees clockwise (top goes to top-right, right goes to bottom-right, and so on) and each end symbol changes to a new symbol. In C the round end at the top must stay a round end at the top-right, and the closed half-circle shape appears at the bottom-right. Option 1 has a round end at top-right and no arrowhead left, so it fits. Options 2 and 4 put a square at the top-right, and options 3 and 5 still keep an arrowhead, so they fail.
trick: First find the turn (here 45 degrees clockwise), then cut options whose end shapes do not match the starting figure.
note: The exact symbol-change rule is not fully clear from the scan; the book answer 1 is used. End symbols (loop, hook, fork, half-disc) are drawn as simplified versions of the scan.
